outline.synopsis: HOOK. Elya Rane discovers a duplicated wartime quarantine/survey shipment manifest personally encrypted by Jacen Solo shortly before his death — same shipment identity, hidden duplicate with conflicting destination data. She remembers the wrong approval field where she once quietly removed fourteen-year-old Ben Skywalker's name and sends him an obsolete GAG-coded message: 'We need to talk. I found something dangerous. It started in GAG. Come alone.' Aevyn Soris arrives. Uses a Jacen-derived blend of memory pressure, Recognition, and Holding to extract what she knows — precise, intimate, controlled rather than showy. Pushes her past what mind and body can survive. Elya dies. The damaged manifest fragment she preserved remains beyond what Aevyn fully extracts. (Consolidated opening hook — formerly Chs 1+2; one sustained chapter through Elya's POV to her death.)

Ben at Shedu Maad, lonely and quietly restless among peers who go careful around his history. HUMANIZING BEAT: small Jedi social/training-space moment before the message — Ben is included in ordinary banter, but the room turns careful once his history is remembered. The obsolete GAG-coded message arrives and unsettles him before the content does. He remembers Elya's small kindness: she once removed his name from a wrong approval field. His hand covers the sender code before he realizes he is hiding it. Briefly orient non-expert readers (Luke's son, Jacen → Caedus, GAG at fourteen, Mara, Order at Shedu Maad).

First Luke holo call. Paternal register — Luke listens, asks two or three quiet questions, classifies the matter as sensitive but not catastrophic. Tells Ben to verify quietly. He is careful because an official Jedi move (which would have to come from Saba and the Council) could relitigate GAG publicly and scatter the trail before there is anything concrete to hold. Ben bristles at being managed. ONE quiet line of post-Crucible texture: Luke looks tired in a way Ben doesn't quite remember, his eyes seem further away even when looking directly at Ben. Ben notices. Ben does NOT ask. Mortis is NEVER named.

INCITING INCIDENT (~11%). Ben arrives too late at Elya's scene. Senses Force-trauma. Recovers the damaged Jacen-sealed duplicate manifest fragment — duplicated shipment identity, quarantine/survey disguise, Jacen's personal encryption marker, partial GAG logistics/audit trace. The fragment is not enough to solve the case alone; the surviving marker points toward an old GAG transfer-chain scandal Ben cannot interpret.

outline.chapter_title: The Man Who Can Read It
outline.synopsis: Ben and GA Justice contacts cross-reference the surviving GAG audit/handler marker. It points toward the same kind of transfer-chain scandal tied to Talon Veyr's conviction. Ben identifies Talon as the person likely to recognize the shipment fraud pattern, not as a magic decoder. Ben does the responsible thing: tries the legal route first using sealed access. That responsible legal query is what alerts the people watching old GAG case files.

Ben arrives at Tarn Velos Coastal Detention Works, the storm-lashed industrial coastal prison. Moves through processing under a low-profile GA Justice records-auditor cover. Talon is brought in — quick, funny, restless, difficult; recognizes the duplicated manifest fragment as a cloned shipment identity; clocks Ben as Skywalker, Jedi, former GAG. HUMANIZING BEAT: prison habit — Talon sits where he can see the door, counts guards mid-joke, keeps his hands visible, pockets food automatically. End hook: the prison alarm changes pitch; Talon notices it is wrong. (Consolidated arrival + meeting — formerly Chs 7+8.)

Cinderline begins the prison snatch under false procedural cover. Lysa manipulates systems; Talon reads the pattern before Ben can. The first snatch team breaches the wing. Ben breaks cover and saves Talon physically — disabling rather than killing, protecting confused prison staff. His restraint is active, not passive: non-lethal Force work, lightsaber control even when speed would be easier. End hook: Ben can win the fight, but Talon says they are going the wrong way. (Consolidated lockdown + rescue — formerly Chs 9+10.)

EQUALITY BEAT. Talon proves he is partner, not cargo, by reading maintenance routes, storm shutters, camera lag, and prison habits. He complains while saving them — talking is how he keeps fear from becoming visible. Ben saves Talon physically; Talon gets them out operationally. The partnership is forced into existence through action before either admits it. Cinderline adjusts pursuit; pushes them toward the exposed sea-wall route.

FIRST PLOT POINT (~24%). Ben and Talon cross storm-exposed gantries and sea-wall while pursued. Ben protects people; Talon gets them to a skiff. They escape Tarn Velos. Ben has crossed a threshold he cannot uncross — broken cover, freed a convicted prisoner, generated a public crisis, committed to the case in a way that makes return impossible. The forced partnership is the new condition of his life. The escape feels costly, not triumphant.

Aftermath of the escape. Luke begins containing the fallout from a distance, calling in what favors he still has with GA Justice. Talon — exhausted, hunted, defensive — gives Ben the next lead: Iressa Vossk. The valve is closed; he is being shown small kindnesses he does not know how to refuse. ACT TURN: Ben and Talon return to Coruscant together, compromised and hunted. Talon joins not from gratitude but because the attack proves the lie that ruined him was only one layer of something larger.

Ben and Talon return from Tarn Velos under pressure. Luke (off-world at Shedu Maad) is doing what he can from distance. HUMANIZING BEAT: Ben takes Talon to the old Skywalker family apartment on Coruscant as a temporary hideout. The apartment exposes more of Ben's family history than Ben intends — the preserved family holo on a shelf, Luke's quiet stack of old mission logs. Talon jokes until he realizes the room is not funny: makes a small dark joke about the holo, sees Ben's face, stops. Using the recovered fragment and the apartment's old secure terminal, Talon identifies Iressa Vossk as the person who can prove where the hidden duplicate manifest went.

outline.chapter_title: Iressa Vossk Does Not Know You
outline.synopsis: Talon finds Iressa by baiting an old private debt-marker through a legitimate records-correction channel. Ben and Talon interrupt Iressa during an ordinary workday at Civitas Archive Systems. Iressa — former GAG Manifest Integrity Analyst, now respectable — denies knowing Talon before proving she does, moves them away from coworkers/cameras, charges a 'Jedi complication fee,' lies about her exits. HUMANIZING BEAT (Civitas lunchroom): Ben briefly waits in an employee break area; an ordinary Civitas employee notices he looks familiar, can't place him, offers him half a sandwich. Ben takes the food, feels ridiculous with a murder clue in his pocket. End hook: Iressa recognizes the fragment as a cloned shipment identity under quarantine/survey disguise.

Iressa reconstructs the damaged manifest trail using legitimate Civitas tools and hidden old-GAG habits beneath them — not by breaking Jacen's encryption but by reconstructing around it through surrounding records (inspection gaps, correction logs, duplicate cargo seals, quarantine overrides, loading dock scans, archive timestamps). The serious work happens at her secondary cache, a quiet leased space she maintains off-record (established here as a passing detail; will become the target of PP2). Ben, Talon, and Iressa enter the old quarantine archive site. Iressa starts splitting/corrupting data so the enemy cannot get a clean copy. End hook: the archive wakes — someone else has recently queried these buried records. (Consolidated reconstruction + archive entry — formerly Chs 17+18.)

PINCH POINT 1 PART A (~37%). Cinderline hits the archive as a cleanup team — seals exits, wipes cameras, triggers old quarantine protocols, tries to leave no clean version of the room behind. Vara Senn appears as an attached Force specialist. Before taking Iressa hostage, Vara engages Ben in a short, cramped lightsaber clash: blunt Lost Tribe aggression, pressure, fear, domination, taunts. Ben recognizes Lost Tribe footwork and a brief Vestara Khai scar-tissue mention lands. Vara recognizes combat will not quickly work and changes tactics. End hook: Vara senses Iressa has hidden something.

PINCH POINT 1 PART B (~39%). Vara takes Iressa hostage and pressures her memory with a crude dark-side method. Ben sees a Jacen-shaped coercive option that might save Iressa and REFUSES it. Iressa finishes corrupting the enemy's copy and transmits her dying package: (1) the documentary chain Ben would need to bring Saba to make an institutional case, and (2) the strategic revelation that the Vigil intends to use the holocron's Recognition/Deepening/Holding for identity-level influence on high-value targets, with Aevyn as Jacen's surviving student. Iressa dies denying Vara the clean version. Her final beat is herself — practical irritation, file anger, one last debt joke rather than sentimental martyrdom. Restraint cost a life.

MIDPOINT (~42%). Aftermath of Iressa's death. Talon presses Ben about the option he refused; Ben cannot cleanly answer whether it would have worked. They examine Iressa's dying transmission — documentary reconstruction tying the Foundation, Korda, and Iresh together, plus the identity-shaping revelation. Ben does the correct thing first: holo-calls Luke (paternal, careful, directs Ben to Saba), then holo-calls Saba (Barabel gravity, formal review, weeks Ben does not have). Both correct. Both too slow. Ben pivots: keep building the documentary case from Iressa's tools while preparing to act outside official channels. Going to Iresh themselves. The Midpoint reversal is quiet — Ben does not announce it; he simply starts working on what comes next.

Ben visits the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation. Aelia is warm, prepared, legitimate, hard to attack — the charity's public work is real. HUMANIZING BEAT (Aelia genuine charity warmth): she writes a handwritten condolence note while Ben watches; remembers a scholarship recipient by name; notices a veteran's discomfort. CIVILIAN-AWKWARDNESS BEAT: while waiting, Ben is offered tea by a young Foundation staffer; over-explains; catches himself. Aelia beats Ben socially before she is exposed operationally. End hook: Talon spots Bren Korda.

Talon identifies Korda as old GAG security system in respectable clothing. Korda's presence implies the Foundation is operationally compromised by old GAG-linked security and records access. Talon's humor THINS — Korda makes him feel contaminated by his own past. Using Iressa's tools, Talon submits a fake manifest correction / records query that makes it look as if a missing piece of the Jacen-sealed duplicate manifest has resurfaced. The signal is boring enough to look bureaucratic, specific enough that anyone guarding the old shipment trail will notice. Talon willingly re-enters the room that ruined his life because the only way to catch the people who put him there is to look like them again. End hook: Korda responds indirectly. (Consolidated Korda-spotted + trap-set — formerly Chs 23+24.)

Ben and Talon follow Korda's response through a Coruscant logistics annex / civic archive loading dock / restricted transit bay. The trail leads to a restricted Foundation/Greyline transfer node. They nearly corner Korda. Korda triggers a prepared escape (lockdown, false emergency, diversion). Ben and Talon still capture a physical proof object — a restricted field authorization / cargo manifest / courier cylinder / datapad pointing to an offworld Foundation mission. Korda is not guarding a dead file; he is guarding an active operation. End hook: Destination — Iresh. The operation is already moving. (Consolidated chase + capture — formerly Chs 25+26.)

outline.pov_character: Tess / Ben / Talon (split — open with Tess)
outline.synopsis: PINCH POINT 2 — THE SQUEEZE (~53%). Three antagonist-pressure beats compound within hours. BEAT 1 (Tess POV): Tess clears the board — orders Korda's elimination as public fall-guy ('Korda was becoming visible. This cleans the board.'); orders Iresh accelerated specifically because Skywalker and Veyr are involved. The acceleration is calculation, not panic. BEAT 2 (Ben + Talon): they return to Iressa's secondary cache to find it raided and burned — no bodies, no witnesses, the documentary case for Saba unrecoverable. The professionalism is the threat; the breach point is not identifiable. BEAT 3 (Talon close): a warrant goes out for Talon on a current Coruscant crime he could not have committed — planted biometric/comm signature, frame constructed with Tess's tradecraft fingerprint. Talon recognizes the work and goes cold. Simultaneously reads public freight indicators showing Cinderline has accelerated Iresh staging past their captured timeline. Documentary path closed, legal cover destroyed, timeline destroyed. RELOCATION to the Skywalker apartment. SECOND LUKE HOLO CALL: brief, quiet; Luke says he will do what he can from where he is; ends without resolution but with Luke knowing what Ben has decided.

From the apartment, Ben and Talon watch news coverage frame Korda as the rogue center of the scandal. Aelia is pressured toward stepping down to preserve the Foundation. The public version of events is already calcifying — and it is incompatible with anything Ben could prove in the time remaining. End hook: Ben, Talon, and Luke (by holo) see the public story is too neat. The cover is moving faster than the truth.

Talon tells Ben more about Tess, Operation Glasshook, Operation Nightglass, Marael Sen, and the remembered GAG corridor moment: 'Move her first.' Not a lore dump — Talon letting Ben see where Tess placed him and why that still burns. Tess was Talon's mentor; reassigned him out of field duty after Glasshook as punishment and 'education,' intending to teach him to see the whole operation. The war collapsed before Tess could bring him back. Talon avoids the truth before he says it — fixes a device that is not broken, changes the subject, eats too fast, jokes badly, then stops. Possible line: 'He said field work had made me sentimental. Logistics would teach me scale.' / 'Did it?' / 'It taught me how easy it is to lose people in paperwork.' End hook: if Tess is involved, Iresh is not a theory; it is an operation.

Ben and Talon confirm the offworld destination and finalize the off-grid transit plan. Luke can only offer limited quiet support without making the case official. They prepare to leave. ACT TURN: Ben and Talon leave for Iresh, knowing the Vigil/Foundation is already moving to recover something Jacen left there.

Ben and Talon arrive on Iresh. The Foundation/Vigil expedition is already present under legitimate cover. The book's texture shifts from Coruscant conspiracy to strange-world expedition: wind, pale cliffs, dark water, chimes, black reeds, thin settlement lights, suspicious locals, too much quiet. A local contact sends them to Sela Dray. HUMANIZING BEAT (Sela ordinary local responsibility): Sela is repairing a chime line, arguing over supply access, or dealing with someone asking about Tavi. Sela refuses Ben and Talon at first — offworlders have already harmed her home. Tavi Dray is missing after taking Foundation money or pressure to guide the expedition. Sela eventually agrees because finding Tavi and stopping the offworlders overlap. End hook: Sela agrees on her terms, not theirs. (Consolidated arrival + Sela refusal — formerly Chs 31+32.)

Sela guides them through Iresh and demonstrates local rules around memory-heavy places. Iresh does not cause madness; the danger is forcing memory/identity pressure into resonance. ONE plain explanation: Iresh did not show the future. It held moments too strongly, like footprints pressed into wet clay. Sela warns them not to trust what they feel just because it feels strong. End hook: they find signs of the Foundation operation near taboo ground.
Ben, Talon, and Sela observe the Foundation/Vigil field camp: legitimate-looking survey work with Cinderline/Greyline security underneath. End hook: Ben senses Aevyn's Force presence.
Ben encounters Aevyn directly or semi-directly. No full fight yet. Aevyn reveals personal knowledge of Jacen and unsettles Ben. End hook: Aevyn confirms Jacen left something near the Glasswell.

HUMANIZING BEAT (Tavi present before endangered). Sela finds evidence Tavi is alive or recently alive near the Glasswell exclusion zone — a guide token, field recorder, damaged pack, warning mark, altered path sign, or practical note. The evidence reveals personality, not just plot: Tavi jokes, complains about Sela being right too often, promises to pay someone back, or leaves a practical warning that shows he knew the risk but needed the money. Cinderline pressure the group. Sela's anger cracks into fear. End hook: the expedition begins moving heavy equipment toward the Glasswell.

SECOND PLOT POINT (~76%). The group discovers Jacen's cache was hidden in old offworld survey/GAG storage equipment near the Glasswell, not in a mystical altar. Talon recognizes the storage logic. Ben recognizes the Force wrongness. Sela recognizes the local danger. When they scan the outer data layers, Ben CONFIRMS what Iressa told them at the Midpoint: the holocron is unfinished, containing Jacen's work on Recognition, Deepening, and Holding — exactly the identity-shaping techniques the Vigil intends to weaponize with Aevyn's help. SPP function is embodiment, not revelation. There is no way to stop Aevyn from getting at the holocron cleanly. The only options left are rescue (saving Tavi and locals from what Aevyn's work is about to break) and denial (keeping Aevyn from leaving with the full prize). End hook: Aevyn begins forcing the cache open. The Glasswell starts to answer.

Aevyn uses Jacen-derived techniques to force the cache open. The Glasswell initially seems beautiful and responsive, then destabilizes. Aevyn is not simply unlocking the cache; he is making the place remember the moment Jacen sealed it. THE GLASSWELL ANSWERS — and the corridor flashback surfaces in Aevyn's POV as fragment, never as exposition or speech: side console, Recognition exercise, Jacen looking up, 'Good. Keep going. We'll review later.' Tavi is trapped or revealed below as water begins entering and the scaffold/mineral supports fail. End hook: the cavern cracks and water begins entering.

CLIMAX PART A — RESCUE FIRST (~82%). Ben tries the ordinary Jedi path during the collapse. It is too slow. Remembering Iressa emotionally rather than philosophically, he acts decisively with Jacen-shaped crisis clarity and saves lives. Ben sees bodies, exits, water, weight, and panic the way Jacen taught him to see crisis. Some people are grateful; some are shaken by how it felt to be moved or commanded. Ben's dangerous choice comes from compassion and urgency, not aggression. The rescue is clearly heroic before it becomes unsettling. End hook: Aevyn recognizes the pattern. Jacen taught Ben that.

CLIMAX PART B — DUEL SECOND (~84%). Aevyn turns fully on Ben. His unstable cold white-blue blade becomes the first sustained lightsaber duel of the book. The duel happens across the collapsing Glasswell: rising water, cracking pale mineral, broken survey scaffolds, mirror-lake reflections, the unstable holocron cache nearby. Aevyn's blade fractures more visibly when Ben uses Jacen-derived logic successfully — visual tell, NOT exposition. The fight is two students of Jacen arguing through action over what his lessons mean. Aevyn uses a technique that hits something buried in Ben. Ben wins by using what Jacen taught him WITHOUT surrendering ownership of himself — does not violate Aevyn's mind, does not pretend Jacen taught him nothing real. End hook: Aevyn is defeated as the Glasswell gives way. (Consolidated duel + victory — formerly Chs 40+41; one sustained climax beat.)

The Glasswell collapses/floods. Ben secures the holocron. Sela and Tavi survive. Talon disrupts Greyline extraction and reroutes escape logistics. Aevyn is presumed dead. Talon's climax job: identify Greyline's emergency extraction beacon; realize they plan to abandon locals; sabotage the beacon; reroute a lift for evacuees; steal a Greyline access cylinder. Sela's climax job: save Tavi and locals through knowledge Ben does not have — taboo side path used by old guides, chimes stopping meaning water pressure shifting, mineral ledges that hold weight. End hook: the Iresh operation is broken; the holocron is in Ben's possession.

Iresh aftermath. Sela remains wary but respects Ben conditionally. Tavi survives but is shaken. HUMANIZING BEAT (Sela/Tavi imperfect reunion): anger, relief, practical care, no easy sentimentality. Talon suspects Ben's holocron decision is not clean. Ben's omission BEGINS here, before the coda — the holocron is unfinished Jacen work (notes, methods, warnings, dangerous knowledge that may also be useful). End hook: they return to Coruscant with the case mostly resolved and the dangerous knowledge unresolved.

Aelia steps down in public disgrace to preserve the Foundation's legitimate charitable work — 'to preserve the Foundation's legitimate work' (her phrasing, public-facing). Korda is the official dead fall guy. The Foundation's lawyers buffer Aelia from criminal liability. Private moral collapse visible but unspoken; she does not recant. End hook: Ben knows the public story is incomplete.

Ben has returned to Shedu Maad after Iresh. First in-person Luke conversation since the holo calls. Luke asks about the holocron. Ben says it is gone, then clarifies only that it is somewhere it cannot hurt anyone. Luke senses the incompleteness and does not force the answer. Ben privately justifies learning what he needs before disposing of it. He is not lying. He is not telling the truth either. He keeps his voice steady, but his hand tightens around the edge of the table as he answers. EXCHANGE: 'The holocron?' / 'Gone.' / 'Gone where?' / 'Somewhere it can't hurt anyone.' / 'That wasn't what I asked.' / 'I know.' End hook: Luke senses the incompleteness but does not force the answer.

Tess survives and retreats deeper into One Sith service. The hand learns Iresh failed and does not panic. Dorvan remains a future target, not a Book 1 puppet. ALLANA REFERENCE: one oblique mention of 'the Hapan question' / 'the unresolved succession thread' in the adversary's review of unresolved assets — Allana NEVER named on-page. End hook: the larger game adjusts.
Far below the broken Glasswell, where the floodwater has gone still, a cold white-blue spark flickers once in the dark. Final image: Aevyn survived, changed.

brooks_alignment.part_1_setup: Chs 1-9 (~24%). Coruscant + Tarn Velos. Elya Rane's discovery and murder by Aevyn opens the central mystery; Ben recovers the damaged Jacen-encrypted manifest fragment; Ben tries the legal route to reach Talon Veyr in prison and is forced into a rescue when Cinderline arrives. The Lie (Ben's: the GAG year has been categorized away) is established and reinforced. Closes with Ben breaking cover at the storm-line escape.
brooks_alignment.inciting_incident: Ch 4 (~11%) 'Not Well' — Ben arrives too late at Elya's murder scene, senses Force-trauma, and recovers the damaged Jacen-sealed duplicate manifest fragment. The case becomes Ben's.
brooks_alignment.first_plot_point: Ch 9 (~24%) 'Storm Line' — Ben and Talon cross storm-exposed gantries and sea-wall while pursued. Ben broke cover, freed a convicted prisoner, generated a public crisis. The forced partnership with Talon is the door Ben cannot return through. Within the canonical 20-25% Brooks window.
brooks_alignment.part_2_response: Chs 10-15 (~25-39%). Coruscant. Ben and Talon become a real investigative pair: Iressa Vossk at Civitas Archive Systems reconstructs the manifest trail; the GAG quarantine archive yields enough to point at the Foundation. Cinderline + Vara hit the archive; Iressa dies after Ben refuses the Jacen-shaped coercive move.
brooks_alignment.first_pinch_point: Chs 14-15 (~37-39%) 'Cleanup Team' / 'The Bad Way' — Cinderline archive cleanup with Vara Senn as Force specialist. Vara/Ben short ugly lightsaber clash, then Vara takes Iressa hostage. Ben refuses the Jacen-shaped coercive move. Iressa dies actively denying Vara a clean copy and transmitting the two-part dying package. The antagonist shows organized lethality; restraint costs the first life.
brooks_alignment.midpoint: Ch 16 (~42%) 'No Good Version' — Iressa's transmission carries the documentary chain AND the identity-shaping revelation (the Vigil intends to use the holocron's Recognition/Deepening/Holding with Aevyn's help). Ben holo-calls Luke, then Saba: both correct, both too slow. Ben pivots from investigator to active disruptor — going to Iresh themselves. Slightly early of canonical 50% but compounded with PP1 in the same chapter.
brooks_alignment.part_3_attack: Chs 17-30 (~45-79%). Coruscant + Iresh transit + Iresh. Ben goes on offense: visits the Foundation and meets Aelia (social defeat); Talon spots Korda; Talon's manifest-correction bait surfaces Korda; chase leads to Iresh evidence. PP2 Squeeze closes every door. Off-grid transit. Iresh arrival, Sela alliance, Tavi seeded, Aevyn confronted, the cache discovered.
brooks_alignment.second_pinch_point: Ch 20 (~53%) 'Containment' — THE SQUEEZE. Three-part compounding pressure within hours: (1) Tess kills Korda as public fall guy and orders Iresh acceleration because Skywalker and Veyr are now involved; (2) Iressa's secondary cache is professionally raided and burned — the documentary case for Saba is unrecoverable, breach point unidentified; (3) Talon is framed for a current Coruscant crime with Tess's tradecraft fingerprint. Documentary path closed, legal cover destroyed, timeline destroyed. Relocation to the Skywalker apartment as final refuge. Slightly early of canonical 62-75% but compounds with PP1+Midpoint to deliver maximum pressure into Act 3's run-up.
brooks_alignment.second_plot_point: Ch 29 (~76%) 'The Cache Site' — at the Glasswell, Ben confirms what Iressa told them at the Midpoint — the holocron's unfinished Recognition/Deepening/Holding work, Aevyn's presence as surviving student, the Vigil's intent. EMBODIMENT not revelation: the known threat becomes concrete. Only options left are rescue and denial. Within the canonical window.
brooks_alignment.part_4_resolution: Chs 31-38 (~82-100%). The Glasswell. Climax + flood + Iresh aftermath + Coruscant coda. Ben uses Jacen-shaped crisis logic to save Tavi and locals; defeats Aevyn in the consolidated duel; secures the unfinished holocron. Aelia steps down. Korda is the dead fall guy. Luke senses Ben's incomplete answer. Tess survives. White-blue spark in the dark.
brooks_alignment.climax: Chs 31-32 (~82-84%) 'Too Slow' / 'What He Left' — Ch 31 rescue first (Ben saves Tavi, Sela's locals, others through Jacen-shaped crisis logic; Aevyn recognizes the pattern); Ch 32 duel second (consolidated lightsaber duel across the collapsing Glasswell, two students of Jacen arguing through action). Ben wins by refusing to let Jacen own what he does with the lessons. The climax functions as ONE sustained beat rather than two.

structural_notes._scene_count_discipline: 38 chapters total. Most chapters carry ONE load-bearing scene. Multi-scene split-POV chapters (Ch 7, 9, 14-15, 16, 20, 33) earn the split because each scene carries a distinct turning point, mission, and emotional arc. Locked humanizing beats (Ch 2, 6, 11, 12, 17, 24, 28, 34) are woven into existing chapters as scene-level character texture, NOT separate scenes or chapters. Chapter Outlines v4.0 consolidated 9 chapter pairs from v3.3's 47-chapter draft — see continuity_note fields per consolidated chapter.
structural_notes._consolidation_history: v4.0 consolidations from v3.3 (47 -> 38 chapters): old Ch 1+2 -> new Ch 1 (Elya hook); old Ch 7+8 -> new Ch 6 (prison arrival + visitor room); old Ch 9+10 -> new Ch 7 (Cinderline attack + Ben break-cover); old Ch 12 (Rusk POV) dropped; old Ch 17+18 -> new Ch 13 (reconstruction + archive entry); old Ch 23+24 -> new Ch 18 (Korda spotted + trap set); old Ch 25+26 -> new Ch 19 (chase + capture); old Ch 31+32 -> new Ch 24 (Iresh arrival + Sela refuses); old Ch 40+41 -> new Ch 32 (duel + victory as continuous climax). FPP shifted from 30% to 24% by the consolidation, landing inside the canonical Brooks 20-25% window.
structural_notes._act_structure: Three-act + coda. Act 1 Chs 1-10 (murder, clue, legal approach, prison break, Ben/Talon partnership forced into being); Act 2 Chs 11-23 (Coruscant investigation, Iressa death, Foundation/Vigil reveal, Korda/Tess escalation, Iresh lead); Act 3 Chs 24-34 (Iresh expedition, Sela/Tavi stakes, Aevyn, Glasswell collapse, duel, holocron recovered); Coda Chs 35-38 (public containment, Ben's morally incomplete holocron choice, One Sith adjustment, Aevyn survival hint).

subplots.name: Talon / Tess Mentor Wound (Glasshook → PP2 frame)
subplots.function: Character-driven antagonist thread; the ownership wound between Talon Veyr and his former GAG mentor Colonel Maro Tess
subplots.arc_summary: Talon's prison habits (Ch 6) carry the wound silently. The FPP rescue (Ch 9) puts him back in motion. The apartment beat (Ch 11) cracks the performance. PP2 Squeeze (Ch 20) puts Tess's tradecraft fingerprint on Talon's frame — the mentor reaching across years to mark him again. Talon names Glasshook and the corridor moment 'Move her first' to Ben in Ch 22 — the wound out loud for the first time. Talon disrupts Greyline extraction at the Glasswell (Ch 33), speaking back to Tess's lesson through field work. Tess survives in Ch 37; the wound persists into Book 2.

subplots.name: Iressa's Rebuilt Respectable Life (Civitas → secondary cache)
subplots.function: Short-arc character subplot carrying the Midpoint structural pivot
subplots.arc_summary: Iressa is introduced at Civitas under her clean professional name (Ch 12); the lunchroom beat humanizes her workplace. Her secondary cache is established as a passing detail (Ch 13) — the off-record space where she does the serious reconstruction. Old GAG instincts wake at the archive (Ch 13-14). She dies preserving the dying package (Ch 15), her short arc resolving: old Iressa buried discrepancies; new Iressa preserved one. The cache is professionally raided and burned at PP2 (Ch 20) — the documentary case she died protecting is overtaken anyway. Her work outlives the body by minutes; the Midpoint pivot (Ch 16) is what her death made possible.

subplots.name: Sela & Tavi / Iresh Local Damage
subplots.function: Act 3 grounding subplot — keeps Iresh a place before it is a metaphor
subplots.arc_summary: Iresh has been damaged by offworlders before. Sela's stake is Tavi, pressured/paid by the Foundation into the Glasswell exclusion zone. Sela refuses to help at first (Ch 24); her conditional alliance comes through specific local knowledge shared without granting offworlder ownership of her home. She demonstrates Iresh's memory-preservation rules through survival vocabulary (Ch 25), not Force theory. Tavi is humanized through evidence — guide tokens, recordings, warning marks — before he becomes a rescue objective (Ch 28). Sela saves Tavi and locals at the Glasswell through knowledge Ben does not have (Ch 31, 33). Imperfect Sela/Tavi reunion (Ch 34): anger, relief, practical care, no easy sentimentality. 'You saved him. That does not make this place yours.'

subplots.name: Aelia's Grief-and-Corruption Entanglement
subplots.function: Public-face antagonist subplot — the Foundation's real charity entangled with the Vigil's hidden ideology
subplots.arc_summary: Aelia beats Ben socially at the Foundation (Ch 17) because her warmth and the charity's public work are real. Korda's presence (Ch 17-18) reveals the operational machinery beneath. Talon's manifest-correction bait surfaces Korda (Ch 18); the chase exposes an active operation (Ch 19). Tess kills Korda at PP2 (Ch 20) — Aelia sees that her cause is being managed by men who treat people as logistics. The news coverage (Ch 21) calcifies a story incompatible with Ben's evidence. Iresh fails (Ch 33). Aelia steps down quietly with no criminal liability (Ch 35) — she accepts the bleaker truth without publicly recanting. The harm persists; the Foundation survives diminished.

subplots.name: Foundation / Vigil Operational Machinery (Cinderline / Greyline / Korda)
subplots.arc_summary: Aevyn's Ch 1 method (precision rather than savagery) signals the operational level. Cinderline's prison snatch (Ch 7) and archive cleanup (Ch 14-15) establish the contractor arm. Korda's spotting at the Foundation (Ch 17) names the old-GAG-in-respectable-clothing layer. Talon's bait + Korda chase (Ch 18-19) yields the Iresh operational evidence. Tess's PP2 board-clearing (Ch 20) — Korda dead, Iressa's cache burned, Talon framed — is the machinery at peak operational tempo. The Iresh field camp (Ch 26) is the apparatus deployed. Aevyn forces the cache (Ch 30); the duel (Ch 32) and flood (Ch 33) collapse the operation. Foundation survives diminished in Ch 35; the machinery outlives this operation in Ch 37.

subplots.name: One Sith Long Game (off-page hand; Aevyn survival)
subplots.function: Series-spanning subplot — glimpsed in Book 1, drives Book 2+ setup
subplots.arc_summary: The One Sith on Korriban remain in patient pre-emergence under Darth Krayt. Tess's PP2 logistics (Ch 20) carry the hand's interest. The Ch 37 hand-POV coda registers Iresh as a failed but recoverable operation in a broader infiltration program. The oblique 'Hapan question' reference (Ch 37) plants Allana as future-target asset without naming her. The Ch 38 cold white-blue spark confirms Aevyn survived: stripped of the holocron, the Vigil, Tess's protection, and the identity of Jacen's unfinished student — broken-open but not destroyed. The cycle continues into Book 2.

hooks.description: Why did Jacen Solo personally encrypt a duplicated wartime shipment manifest days before Shedu Maad, and why did the hidden copy go somewhere the public shipment never went? Reader-facing form: why did one of Jacen's last shipments have two lives? Resolved at the Midpoint when Iressa's dying transmission reveals the holocron's identity-shaping purpose.
Who killed Elya Rane, and what is the precision of the method? The Force-trauma Ben senses in Ch 4 names the killer through behavior. Aevyn is unsettled into semi-revelation in Ch 27.

Is Talon Veyr the right partner, or has Ben made a catastrophic mistake breaking cover for him? The storm-line escape answers through action: Ben saves Talon physically, Talon gets them out operationally.

Whom is the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation actually protecting? Korda's spotting in Ch 17, manifest-correction bait in Ch 18, and Korda chase in Ch 19 resolve the operational connection: the Foundation is guarding an active Iresh operation.

Why is the Vigil moving on Iresh NOW? The SPP at the cache site confirms: because Aevyn can finish the holocron, because Ben's involvement accelerates the timeline, and because the cache has always been on Iresh waiting for the right student.

Can Ben use Jacen's lessons without becoming Caedus? PP1 Iressa death plants the question (restraint cost a life); Ch 31 Glasswell rescue tests it (the lessons save lives); Ch 32 duel resolves it (Ben wins by using what Jacen taught him WITHOUT surrendering ownership).

Who told Cinderline where Iressa's secondary cache was? The breach point at PP2 is deliberately not identified. A coworker leaned on? A forgotten contact? A small breach Iressa herself never noticed? The unanswered version is creepier and serves the novel's institutional-decay theme. Available as a Book 2 thread or as ambient unanswered weight.

What does Ben do with the preserved unfinished holocron? Luke senses the omission in Ch 36 and does not force the answer. Talon suspects in Ch 34 and names it in Ch 34. The answer belongs to Book 2 — the cycle of Ben's morally compromised choices continuing.

Did Aevyn really survive, and what does he become after the broken certainty? Ch 38's cold white-blue spark confirms survival to the reader only — Ben, Talon, and the Order presume him dead. Book 2 seed: possible Bane-like emergence from a broken order; possible rival-student alliance against something worse.

revelation_schedule.what: The duplicated wartime quarantine/survey shipment manifest exists, personally encrypted by Jacen Solo shortly before his death.
revelation_schedule.impact: Opens the central mystery and Ben's investigation.

revelation_schedule.what: Aevyn killed Elya using a precise Jacen-derived method (memory pressure, Recognition, Holding) — precision rather than savagery.
revealed_to: Ben (partial — senses Force-trauma but does not yet know the killer's identity)
revelation_schedule.impact: Frames the antagonist's mythic register through behavior before name; reader knows the method links to Jacen before Ben does.

revelation_schedule.what: Jacen's personal encryption marker is on the fragment Ben recovers — this is not a clerical duplicate.
revelation_schedule.impact: Makes the case personal — Ben is investigating his cousin's last work.

revelation_schedule.what: The fragment is a cloned shipment identity under quarantine/survey disguise — someone dressed a secret up as medical cargo.
revelation_schedule.impact: Reframes the duplicate from clerical accident to deliberate concealment; advances the investigation.

revelation_schedule.what: The Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation is operationally compromised — Bren Korda, old GAG security, is guarding the buried shipment trail.
revelation_schedule.impact: Connects the public charity to the conspiracy; reframes Aelia.

revelation_schedule.what: The holocron is Jacen's unfinished work on Recognition, Deepening, and Holding — identity-shaping techniques. The Vigil intends to weaponize them for identity-level influence on high-value targets, with Aevyn as the only surviving student who can finish the work.
revelation_schedule.impact: The Midpoint revelation. Reframes the case from murder investigation to civilizational stakes — and gives Ben the strategic clarity to pivot from investigator to active disruptor.
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Iressa's reconstruction work (Ch 13) must demonstrate she has the records-trade competence to assemble this picture before her death.

revelation_schedule.what: Aevyn was Jacen Solo's surviving Force student from the GAG/Caedus period — the other student.
revelation_schedule.impact: Sets up the duel as argument-through-action between two students of Jacen.

revelation_schedule.what: Colonel Maro Tess is the operational architect of the Vigil's field operations — and Talon's former GAG mentor.
revelation_schedule.impact: Names the calm operational center of the conspiracy; sets up Talon/Tess as the ownership-wound subplot.

revelation_schedule.what: Tess's tradecraft fingerprint is on the Coruscant frame that puts a warrant out for Talon — specific cover-identity construction patterns, particular evidence routing.
revelation_schedule.impact: Personal: Tess is reaching across years to mark Talon again. Closes Luke's legal cover; forces off-grid Iresh transit.

revelation_schedule.what: Jacen's cache is hidden in old offworld survey / GAG-era storage equipment near the Glasswell — practical, deniable, Jacen-like — NOT a Sith temple, Jedi ruin, or mystical altar.
revelation_schedule.impact: SPP embodiment of the Midpoint revelation. The threat the reader has known about since Ch 15 becomes physically inescapable.

revelation_schedule.what: Aevyn's corridor wound: Jacen leaving a Recognition session with him to walk off with fourteen-year-old Ben, the 'later' that never came. Aevyn was the side project who lived in the gaps.
revelation_schedule.impact: Surfaces in Aevyn's Ch 30 POV as image only — NEVER as exposition, NEVER as speech. Ben never learns it; the wound stays in adversary awareness as the engine of the duel.
revelation_schedule.setup_required: Aevyn's behavior across Ch 1, Ch 14-15, Ch 27 must establish the precision and the woundedness without ever naming the cause.

revelation_schedule.what: Ben preserved the unfinished holocron after the Glasswell — did not destroy it, did not hand it over cleanly to the Order. He preserves it under a technically-true omission.
revealed_to: Talon (suspects in Ch 34; names it without rupturing)
Luke (senses incompleteness in Ch 36; does not force the answer)
revelation_schedule.impact: The book's central moral compromise. Ben's omission begins in Act 3 (Ch 33-34), is named privately by Talon in Ch 34, and lands at the Ch 36 'Gone where?' coda exchange with Luke. The most defensible choices and the most dangerous choices can be the same choices.

revelation_schedule.what: Aevyn survived the Glasswell collapse, broken-open and changed — stripped of the holocron, the Vigil, Tess's protection, and the identity of Jacen's unfinished student.
revelation_schedule.impact: Series hook. Ben, Talon, Sela, the Order all presume Aevyn dead. The cold white-blue spark in the dark is the Book 2 cycle beginning.

revelation_schedule.what: The One Sith on Korriban under Darth Krayt remain in patient pre-emergence; Wynn Dorvan is a future target of an identity-shaping infiltration program of which Iresh was one chess move; the broader game continues. The 'Hapan question' (Allana as adversary-awareness asset) is part of that program.
revelation_schedule.impact: Series hook. Names the long game without lifting the One Sith veil; positions Dorvan and Allana as Book 2+ stakes without bringing either on-page.

promise_payoff_ledger.promise: Why did one of Jacen's last shipments have two lives? — the central mystery.
The forced Ben/Talon partnership will outlast the case as a real partnership — not a transaction.
Restraint can cost lives — Ben will learn this not as a philosophical position but as a body lying still after he held the line.
Every door except Iresh will be closed — the institutional path, the documentary path, the legal path, the time path. Ben will go off-grid because there is no other door.
Ben will use Jacen's lessons — the crisis logic the GAG year built into him will save lives that the ordinary Jedi path cannot save.

Aelia Vandros will be socially formidable AND publicly diminished — the Foundation's real charity will be the reason Ben cannot morally flatten her, AND the reason her stepping down preserves the harm.
Sela will save Tavi and the locals through specific Iresh knowledge Ben does not have — the climax rescue will be a shared act of different competencies.
Talon will name his Glasshook/Tess wound out loud — the prison habits and the comedy valve are the cover for a confession that has to land in Ben's hearing in his own register.
Ben will preserve the unfinished holocron under a technically-true omission — his most defensible and most dangerous choice will be the same choice.
Aevyn will survive the Glasswell — the precision method that opens the book will outlast the operation that deployed it.
The One Sith long game will continue — Iresh was one chess move; Dorvan and the broader infiltration program survive Book 1's case being closed.
Luke will sense the omission and not force the answer — the father who knows is the strongest indictment the book can offer.
